### T08e56ae20787a380767b49bd

```text
Whereas, in my judgment, the public interest requires that Harry T. Edwards, senior technologist, Bureau of Plant Industry, Department of Agriculture, who was exempted from compulsory retirement for age for periods totaling two years by Executive Orders No. 8259 of September 21, 1939, and No. 8525 of August 26, 1940, be further exempted from such compulsory retirement for a period of one year:

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (U.S.C., title 5, sec. 715a), I hereby further exempt the said Harry T. Edwards from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending October 31, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

July 24, 1941.

```

### T0e751fca7fe4999853a5a787

Text hash ffe43d29f8d3c2ce427fad30538bf17803a96ded9aa0581c6b5feb4c9b515a00; absolute characters 0–1321; files: jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-7863-exemption-frank-b-bourn-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt

```text
Whereas section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, 47 Stat. 382, 404 (5 U.S.C., sec. 715a), provides:

"On and after July 1, 1932, no person rendering civilian service in any branch or service of the United States Government or the municipal government of the District of Columbia who shall have reached the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to such person, shall be continued in such service, notwithstanding any provision of law or regulation to the contrary: Provided, That the President may, by Executive Order, exempt from the provisions of this section any person when, in his judgment, the public interest so requires * * *";

And Whereas the public interest requires that Frank B. Bourn, Chief of the Supplies and Accounts Division, Office of the Secretary of War, War Department, who, during the month of June, 1938, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, be exempted from the provisions of this section and continued in the service until July 1, 1939;

Now, Therefore, by virtue of and pursuant to the authority vested in me by the aforesaid section, I do hereby exempt Frank B. Bourn from the provisions thereof and continue him in the service until July 1, 1939.

FRANKLIN D. ROOSEVELT

The White House,

April 7, 1938.

```

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

June 25, 1941.

Thompson, Chief, Mechanical Engineering Section, Office of the Supervising Architect, Public Buildings Administration, Federal Works Agency, who, during the month of September, 1940, will reach the retirement age prescribed for automatic separation from the service, applicable to him, be exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year:

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

May 7, 1940.

```

Andrews from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941.

FRANKLIN D ROOSEVELT

The White House,

September 28, 1940.

8402 (May 7, 1940, Franklin D. Roosevelt) is a one-paragraph exemption order read in full in the held American Presidency Project transcription (Wayback capture; a provisional working text, grade mirror_transcription). The page record's heading names the number and its date and subject agree with the text. Its only operative command, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932, exempts Nelson S. Thompson from compulsory retirement for age for a stated term: \"I hereby exempt the said Nelson S. Thompson from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending September 30, 1941.\". The term ends September 30, 1941 by its own words. Later exemption orders for the same person are later events and new grants; none revokes or shortens this order.\nMember checks: {\"earlier_end_check\":\"No earlier end is held. A search of the held corpus for the order's number in the form Executive Order No. 8402 found only the later exemption order(s) listed in later_events. No held instrument revokes this exemption before its term ran, and no held source shows the person separated before then.\",\"independent_command_check\":\"No independent command survives. No held source shows any other residual.\",\"scope_check\":\"The order is a single operative paragraph and one clause; the preamble recital of the public interest is not a separate command. I read all 755 characters. APP page check against the mirror record (Common Crawl capture): its heading names Executive Order 8581, its date 1940-10-31 agrees with the signing line of the text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. The held text prints the recital month as November, 1910 (the order is dated October 31, 1940), the operative surname as MeClellan, and \"authority rested in me\"; these are evident misprints that do not touch the stated period. Whole-order status is no (provisional, already adopted; not changed here). The order exempts Andrew MeClellan from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending November 30, 1941 and ends on that stated date. The end is the order's own fixed term, recorded inclusive with the exclusive reading disclosed. No later event is held.
